premise: The public library culls books nobody checks out, so Daria starts borrowing the doomed ones to save them, and realizes she's gaming a popularity metric exactly like the people she despises.
A 2000 census taker reaches the Morgendorffers' door and Daria, answering truthfully, finds that every box on the form describes a family that doesn't exist.
Daria tries to return a defective lamp to Cashman's and is passed up a chain of ever-more-empowered clerks who can't say no or yes.
Andrea, the silent goth, publicly calls Daria a poser misanthrope, and Daria finds herself competing to prove her alienation is authentic.
Daria is accused of secretly taking Tiffany's SAT, and her only alibi is the earnest thing she was actually doing that Saturday, which she would rather be expelled than admit.
Daria's subdivision forms a homeowners' association, and after reading the bylaws she runs for the board to weaponize them against the neighbors.
The Morgendorffers hold a yard sale and Daria, running the cash box, watches strangers haggle the family's past down to a quarter.
Pizza King launches a loyalty card, Daria and Jane turn out to be its most loyal customers in town, and their photo on the wall ends their anonymity.
To test its gullibility, Daria sends Sick Sad World a fabricated tip about Lawndale, and when the crew arrives the whole town eagerly corroborates her invention.
Jodie, burning out, asks Daria to teach her how to stop caring for one week.
Daria loses a bet and must spend a week saying only sincere things, and finds nobody in Lawndale can tell the difference.
Assigned to research Lawndale's founder for the town's anniversary pageant, Daria finds he was a land speculator who invented its history, and the town prefers the invention.
Serving detention in the lost-and-found room, Daria reconstructs Lawndale High's social order from what people abandon.
Daria wins Mrs. Bennett's stock-market game by shorting everything Lawndale loves, and her portfolio reads like a forecast of the town.
Daria gets a 12-step amends letter from her childhood bully and refuses to provide the closure it requires.
The DMV rejects Daria's expressionless license photo, and she must produce a smile acceptable to the state.
Jane's mother Amanda asks to sculpt Daria, and being represented sincerely turns out to be worse than being mocked.
Ms. Li inflates every grade to lift Lawndale's ranking, and Daria fights to get her honest B back.
Daria's petition is signed by everyone, none of whom read it, so she circulates one against it, and that passes too.
Interning at the Lawndale Herald, Daria is put on the police blotter and finds it is the only honest literature the town produces.
Newly 18, Daria votes in a local election and is the only person in her precinct who read the ballot measure.
Trent takes a day job and turns out to be good at it, and Daria's crush can't survive his name tag.
A magazine names Lawndale the Most Average Town in America; the town throws a parade and Daria is the only one insulted.
The Morgendorffers become a Nielsen family, and Daria realizes her viewing now decides what America watches.
A fast-food chain picks Lawndale as its test market for being statistically average, and Daria tries to skew the data.
A freshman copies Daria's look and manner exactly and is instantly popular for it.
As punishment Daria must wear the Lawndale Lions mascot suit, and anonymous inside it she becomes the most beloved figure at school.
Daria spends the entire episode on hold with the phone company while the household orbits her.
Daria's paid focus-group contempt for a new soda becomes its marketing campaign.
Aunt Amy brings Daria to her 20th high-school reunion as a human shield.
Upchuck completes a charm course and becomes impeccably polite, which everyone finds far creepier.
Mack wants to quit football for an AP class, and Daria coaches him on being unpopular while the town's Friday nights panic.
Daria answers the district's anonymous risk survey honestly and becomes the statistical outlier the district panics about.
Helen double-books, so Daria attends Quinn's parent-teacher conference as guardian and hears what the teachers really think of her sister.
Made to read the morning announcements, Daria delivers the scripted cheer verbatim and deadpan, and it becomes a cult hit.
Ms. Li's polygraph is deployed to vet hall passes, and Daria is the only student who passes.
Daria tutors a genuinely happy middle-schooler and fails, over every session, to corrupt her.
Sick Sad World is facing cancellation, and Daria finds herself organizing a fan letter campaign.
Daria contests a parking ticket in traffic court, representing herself.
